michigan_review.source_scope: The raw official report itself is headed “Michigan Department of State | Official Candidate Listing | All State and Judicial Offices | General Election | Tuesday, November 3, 2026”; its U.S. Senate section contains six candidate entries with party and filing method.

extracted_rows_verification.comparison: All six extracted rows match the names, parties, filing methods, and U.S. Senate section in raw/mi-gen2026.html.
extracted_rows_verification.report_literal_case_insensitive_search: The extraction reports zero occurrences of “write” and “declaration”; direct search of the complete saved report HTML also returns no such term.

michigan_review.coverage_assessment: The six rows document the ordinary statewide Senate candidate listing. Their row/table structure has no declaration-of-intent field or explicit write-in-coverage language. Official page labeling `All State and Judicial Offices` describes office scope, not the declaration type or inclusion of write-ins. The report therefore does not establish complete write-in coverage or zero write-in declarations.

primary_manual_check.evidence: The original July 2024 Michigan Bureau of Elections manual, chapter 4, says a public-office write-in candidate generally must file a Declaration of Intent with the appropriate election official by 4 p.m. on the second Friday preceding the election; BOE/county clerk notify local clerks of timely filed write-in candidates. It states that if a candidate dies or is otherwise disqualified after the deadline, the declaration requirement is waived for that office.
primary_manual_check.provenance: PDF is linked from the official Michigan SOS admin-info page; PDF bytes and response headers match receipt pins. The manual file itself displays July 2024; HTTP Last-Modified is 2025-05-19. It does not enumerate 2026 filed candidates.
primary_manual_check.consequence: The manual supports the rule and explains a potential exception; it is not a post-deadline named declaration roster. A separate official BOE or county filing/notification record is still needed for support closure.

michigan_review.concrete_correction_or_limit: Keep the six ordinary listed candidates separate from write-in eligibility. Do not describe the candidate report as a qualified write-in roster, or infer zero from its silence. The disclosed deadline and exception do not fill that roster gap.

montana_review.raw_source_scope: Raw portal HTML heading reads FEDERAL GENERAL 2026. The table header explicitly labels the timestamp column `Filing Date`; it labels the left and hidden right status columns `Status`.
montana_review.row_match: All five extracted rows match raw table rows for UNITED STATES SENATOR, REGULAR, term length 6, District Type Statewide / District STATE. In Jami Dee Woodman's row, both status cells display FILED and the `Filing Date` cell displays 8/7/2026 2:30:07 PM. Raw row also contains literal WRITE-IN in the separate Email/Web Address column; the safe extraction properly omits that contact/display column.
montana_review.key_semantics: The UI provides a displayed `Filing Date` and `FILED` status only. It gives no field definition tying that date to receipt of the legally operative declaration, no linked detail/adjudication for this row, and no certification/qualification status. Treat `FILED` as portal status, not qualified/certified or timely/legal receipt.
montana_review.date_rule_relation: The packet's pinned current MCA 13-10-211/calendar capture states ordinary write-in filing by 5 p.m. on the 90th day before the election, Aug. 5 for Nov. 3, 2026, subject to statutory exceptions. The displayed Aug. 7 timestamp is later than that ordinary date, but field semantics/time zone and any exception/adjudication are unverified. Do not conclude timely/late legal receipt or countability from the display alone.
montana_review.pagination_limit: Raw portal HTML says page size 100 and 272 total items across 3 pages. The five Senate rows are visible at rows 0–4 on the downloaded page; the packet did not retrieve pages 2–3 or a Senate-only total. The receipt accurately says five rows visible; the report's phrasing could be misread as exhaustive. Do not characterize the five as a complete portal-wide Senate roster without a dedicated scope proof.
montana_review.concrete_correction_or_limit: Add the page-count limitation to any downstream description of roster completeness. The named Jami Dee Woodman write-in marker is present in a contact/display cell, but that does not establish legal countability. The portal's date and status remain procedural leads only.

temporal_and_privacy_limits.source_retrieval: Both source packets record retrieval on 2026-10-25, after the owner forecast cutoff 2026-10-20; they do not prove source availability/content at that cutoff.
temporal_and_privacy_limits.derived_privacy: MT extraction omits raw contact and mailing-address columns as declared. This review deliberately reproduces none of those values.
temporal_and_privacy_limits.failed_requests: The failed Michigan Saginaw HEAD request preserved no response body/headers and was not independently verifiable; it is not candidate evidence. Michigan's generic SOS 403 headers are hashed and match, but no error body was preserved.
temporal_and_privacy_limits.no_zero_inference: Neither an ordinary roster's silence (MI) nor the portal view (MT) establishes zero filings, statewide completeness, or legal qualification.

reviewer_conclusion: The hash pins are sound and the extractions match the preserved response content for the fields reviewed. MI stays held for lack of official 2026 write-in declaration coverage. MT is a valid original-portal FILED lead naming a write-in candidate, but the displayed Filing Date, FILED label, and paginated view do not resolve receipt semantics, exceptions, certification, or complete roster coverage.
